tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigated to the Magento admin login, authenticated, then opened Manage Products grid and performed grid filtering, selection and navigation to an Edit page. The stable anchors identified were the Manage Products URL (http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/), column header text (ID, Name, SKU, Price, Qty, Type, Attrib. Set Name, Visibility, Status, Websites), the Search button, and the Edit page URL pattern /admin/catalog_product/edit/id/<id>/.

Task Definition:
- Build a deterministic, re-usable tool that: navigates to the Manage Products grid, fills grid filters with user-provided criteria, runs the grid Search, waits for results, and opens the product Edit page for the provided product id. The tool must use stable selectors (column-anchored XPath or direct edit URL) to avoid fragile positional indexing.

Action Plan (ordered):
1) Navigate to Manage Products grid URL (deterministic). 2) Fill each grid filter control using column-anchored XPaths (ID From/To, Name, SKU, Price From/To, Qty From/To). 3) Set selects (Type, Attribute Set, Visibility, Status, Websites) using visible option text via select_change steps. 4) Click the Search button to apply filters. 5) Wait briefly for results. 6) Open the Edit page for the requested product ID using a deterministic direct URL navigation (replaces brittle per-row clicking). 7) Extract key product fields from the edit page to confirm the correct product loaded.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- product_id_to_edit (required): the ID to open for editing. The tool's main purpose is to open this product's edit page. Derived from recorded actions where the agent opened /edit/id/2784/. 
- id_from, id_to, name, sku, price_from, price_to, qty_from, qty_to, type, attribute_set, visibility, status, website (all optional): match the grid filter controls captured during the session. The names mirror column header names and form field semantics in the grid to avoid mapping layers.

Step Optimization and Determinism:
- Replace brittle per-row Edit link clicking with direct navigation to the edit URL (/admin/catalog_product/edit/id/{id}/). This is deterministic and was specifically used in the session when safe.
- Use column-anchored XPaths (//th[a[normalize-space()='...']]//input/select) to scope filter inputs and selects: these anchor to visible header text so they should remain stable across admin themes and localization (with text adjustments). Where a unique id exists (edit URL or product form inputs like #name, #sku, #price, #qty) prefer those; however, since the product-grid DOM was used for filters, XPaths offer stable scoping.
- No authentication steps included: the session recording authenticated before performing grid interactions. The tool assumes an authenticated browser context per instructions.

Notes and Constraints:
- The tool executes all filter actions without runtime branching; if a parameter is empty the corresponding input will be set to an empty value (clearing the field). This keeps the step sequence deterministic.
- The edit navigation is required (product_id_to_edit is required). This focuses the tool on the single goal: find and open a product for editing.
- If your Magento instance uses localized header texts, substitute the column header text in the XPaths accordingly. If any XPath resolves to multiple elements in your environment, replace with an id-based selector or use the provided edit URL navigation as the most reliable way to open a product.

Justification of included steps:
- All included actions are essential to find products in the grid and open the chosen product for editing. The tool omits mass-action and Add Product steps to keep the tool single-purpose and deterministic (open-for-edit). Those auxiliary flows can be implemented as separate tools if needed.
name: magento_find_and_open_product_tool
description: Search the Magento admin product grid using provided criteria (ID range, Name, SKU, Price range, Qty range, Type, Attribute Set, Visibility, Status, Website) and open a specific product for editing. Assumes an authenticated admin session is already present in the browser context. This tool navigates to the Manage Products grid, fills the grid filters, applies Search, waits for results, then opens the Edit page for the product specified by product_id_to_edit and extracts the product's key fields from the edit page.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento Manage Products grid (starting page).
Enter ID From filter value (left / lower bound). If empty, this will clear the field.
Enter ID To filter value (right / upper bound). If empty, this will clear the field.
Set the Type filter select to the visible option text provided. If empty, no selection is made (select_change will attempt to match empty string and may be a no-op).
Set the Attribute Set filter select to the visible option text provided.
Leave the Price currency select unchanged (most grids default to USD); this step is left blank but guarantees the selector is referenced so automation waits for it to exist.
Set the Visibility filter select to the visible option text provided.
Set the Status filter select to the visible option text provided.
Set the Websites filter select to the visible option text provided.
Click the Search / Apply Filters button to run the filter query on the product grid.
Wait briefly for the grid to refresh with filtered results.
Open the Edit page for the product specified by product_id_to_edit (direct URL navigation is deterministic and avoids brittle per-row indexing).
Capture the Name, SKU, Price, Qty and page title from the product Edit form for verification.
steps.goal: Extract product fields from the edit page: product name, sku, price (prices tab), qty (inventory tab), and confirm page title.

input_schema.name: product_id_to_edit
input_schema.description: Numeric product ID to open for editing (example: "2784"). The tool will navigate directly to the edit URL for this ID after applying filters.

input_schema.name: id_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for product ID filter (grid 'ID From'). Leave empty to not restrict by lower ID.

input_schema.name: id_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for product ID filter (grid 'ID To'). Leave empty to not restrict by upper ID.

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: Text to enter in the Name filter (grid). Exact or partial product name to filter by.

input_schema.name: sku
input_schema.description: Text to enter in the SKU filter (grid). Exact or partial SKU to filter by.

input_schema.name: price_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for Price filter (grid 'Price From'). Use numeric format (e.g. "10").

input_schema.name: price_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for Price filter (grid 'Price To'). Use numeric format (e.g. "100").

input_schema.name: qty_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for Qty filter (grid 'Qty From'). Use numeric format (e.g. "0").

input_schema.name: qty_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for Qty filter (grid 'Qty To'). Use numeric format (e.g. "100").

input_schema.name: type
input_schema.description: Visible text of the Type filter select (e.g. "Simple Product", "Configurable Product"). Leave empty to not change Type filter.

input_schema.name: attribute_set
input_schema.description: Visible text of the Attribute Set filter select (e.g. "Default"). Leave empty to not change Attribute Set filter.

input_schema.name: visibility
input_schema.description: Visible text of the Visibility filter select (e.g. "Catalog, Search"). Leave empty to not change Visibility filter.

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Visible text of the Status filter select ("Enabled" or "Disabled"). Leave empty to not change Status filter.

input_schema.name: website
input_schema.description: Visible text of the Websites filter select (e.g. "Main Website"). Leave empty to not change Websites filter.
